Action Plan:
1. Increase preventer inhaler (Clenil – beclomethasone) from 3 puffs to 4 puffs twice daily until reviewed.
2. Continue reliever inhaler (Salbutamol) up to every 2–4 hours PRN; if use approaches every 2 hours or symptoms deteriorate, seek urgent care.
3. Book face-to-face GP appointment within the next few days for full asthma review, chest examination, and peak-flow assessment; GP to decide on need for oral steroids and/or antibiotics.
4. Attend emergency department immediately if shortness of breath worsens or reliever inhaler is ineffective.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 2–3-day history of shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough, worse with exertion; blue inhaler provides little relief.  
• History of present illness:
  – Onset while running; persists with brisk walking.  
  – No sputum production.  
• Past medical history: Asthma (last severe attack 3–4 years ago; never hospitalized).  
• Last asthma review: ~2 years ago.  
• Family history: Brother with asthma, sister with eczema.  
• Medications:  
  – Clenil (beclomethasone) inhaler 3 puffs twice daily (dose/route/frequency patient-reported; plan to increase).  
  – Salbutamol inhaler PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Cetraben cream (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Hydrocortisone topical (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever); no known drug allergies.  
• Social history: Not discussed.

Objective:
• No physical examination performed during telehealth consult.  
• No vitals recorded.  
• No investigations performed; patient’s usual peak flow reportedly ~380 L/min.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute deterioration of asthma control  
   – Assessment: Mild asthma exacerbation/poor control.  
   – Investigations planned: Peak-flow measurement and chest examination at upcoming GP visit.  
   – Treatment: Increase Clenil to 4 puffs BID; continue Salbutamol up to every 2–4 h PRN.  
   – Referrals/Follow-up: Face-to-face GP appointment within a few days; advise ED attendance if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Current vitals, inhaler technique review, smoking status, detailed medication doses.  
• Internal conflicts: Frequency of Clenil use—patient agreed to “3 puffs twice daily” after clinician suggestion; exact prior dose unclear (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor repetitions and placeholders, no inaudible sections.
